items.title: Why we cure meat with nitrites
items.claim: Sodium nitrite is used in cured meats partly for colour and flavour. What is its main food-safety function?
items.reveal:
C. botulinum produces one of the most lethal toxins known. Nitrites suppress its growth in the anaerobic conditions inside cured meats.

The IARC classified processed meat as Group 1 carcinogenic to humans in 2015 partly due to nitrite and nitrate residues; risks and benefits are now actively traded off in regulation.
items.why: Food additives often combine functional safety roles with health trade-offs.

items.title: PLA composting
items.claim: Polylactic acid (PLA) is often marketed as a compostable bioplastic for food packaging. What is true of its end-of-life conditions?

options.text: It composts in any home compost bin in days
It typically requires industrial composting with controlled temperature and microbes
It does not degrade at all

items.reveal_title: Industrial composting, not the home bin
items.reveal:
PLA is certified under standards such as EN 13432 for industrial composting at around 55-60 C. In landfills and oceans it degrades slowly.

Misclassification of PLA as 'biodegradable' has been a recurring concern in waste streams.
items.why: Sustainability labels require infrastructure to deliver their promised outcomes.

items.title: Coeliac disease prevalence
items.claim: Coeliac disease is an autoimmune reaction to gluten. What is the approximate population prevalence in Western countries based on serological screening?
items.reveal:
Singh et al. (2018, meta-analysis) reported a global pooled seroprevalence of 1.4% and biopsy-confirmed prevalence of 0.7%. Most cases remain undiagnosed.

Non-coeliac gluten sensitivity is a separate, less well-characterised category.
items.why: Population screening reveals that some conditions are far more common than clinic-based estimates suggest.
